ui_bugs.issue: The data-rh='true' attribute on static meta/link tags in public/index.html does NOT cause react-helmet-async v3.0.0 to replace them. Helmet still appends a second tag of each kind on every route. Result: 2x meta[name=description], 2x link[rel=canonical], 2x meta[name=robots], 2x og:title/description/url/image, 2x twitter:title/description/image on every public route.

Both routes still expose meta[name=robots]='index, follow, max-image-preview:large, max-snippet:-1' (static, listed first) in addition to the intended 'noindex, nofollow' (Helmet-appended). Crawlers that honor the first occurrence will index /admin and /portal — the originally reported leak is NOT fixed.

action_items: The data-rh='true' approach is INEFFECTIVE with react-helmet-async v3.0.0 — Helmet v3 does NOT reconcile against existing static DOM tags by that attribute (it only replaces tags it itself has mounted). Pick ONE of the following for a real fix: (a) REMOVE the following from public/index.html entirely so Helmet becomes the single source: meta[name=description], meta[name=robots], link[rel=canonical], og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image, twitter:title, twitter:description, twitter:image (keep title, og:type, og:site_name, og:image dimensions/alt, og:locale, twitter:card, favicon, gtag snippet, JSON-LD); (b) Add a one-time cleanup effect in a root component that removes server-rendered static copies of those tags on mount before Helmet renders; or (c) switch to a Helmet version/approach that supports true hydration takeover of statically-rendered head tags. Option (a) is simplest and was the recommendation from iteration_1 — adding data-rh did not help.
After the above fix, verify /admin and /portal have exactly ONE meta[name=robots] = 'noindex, nofollow'.

rca of the issue: react-helmet-async v3.0.0 inserts head tags via its own render pipeline and tracks what it inserts to replace them on updates. It does NOT scan existing document head for tags marked with data-rh and claim ownership of them — that attribute is written OUT by Helmet (SSR output marker) but is NOT a signal Helmet reads IN during client-side mounting. Therefore, static tags in public/index.html (even with data-rh='true') remain in the DOM alongside Helmet-rendered tags. The only reliable fixes are (a) delete the static duplicates from index.html, or (b) imperatively remove them in a mount effect before Helmet mounts.
